back: An industrial network system for real-time distributed control that connects the instruments in a manufacturing plant.
excerpt: A fieldbus is an industrial network system for real-time distributed control. It is a way to connect instruments in a manufacturing plant.
mnemonic: One bus line running through the 'field' (the plant floor), picking up every instrument on the way.

front: Why does a fieldbus need far less cabling than 4-20 mA wiring to each device?
back: 4-20 mA needs a separate connection point at the controller for every device; a fieldbus carries many analog and digital points through one.
excerpt: which require only one communication point at the controller level and allow multiple of analog and digital points to be connected at the same time

front: What turns ordinary Ethernet into 'industrial Ethernet'?
back: Its use in an industrial environment together with protocols that provide determinism and real-time control.
excerpt: Industrial Ethernet (IE) is the use of Ethernet in an industrial environment with protocols that provide determinism and real-time control.

front: In a Modbus transaction, which device is the client?
back: The device that initiates the transaction by sending a request to a server.
excerpt: Modbus defines a client which is an entity that initiates a transaction to request any specific task from its request receiver.

front: Older Modbus documents speak of a master and slaves. Which of them is today's client?
back: The master is the client; each slave is a server.
excerpt: In former terminology, the client was named master and the server named slave.
mnemonic: The master gives the orders, so the master is the one who asks: the client.

front: Why must a Modbus client keep polling its field devices to notice changes?
back: A server never transmits on its own initiative; it only answers requests, so the client has to ask again and again.
excerpt: A slave will never transmit any data or perform any action without a request from the master, and slaves cannot communicate with each other.

front: In the Modbus data model, what is a coil?
back: A single-bit data item that a client can both read and write.
excerpt: Coils Single bit Read-Write Input Registers 16-bit word Read-Only
mnemonic: Named after the relay coil of ladder logic: one bit you can switch on or off.

front: How does a Modbus discrete input differ from a coil?
back: Both are single bits, but a discrete input is read-only, while a coil can also be written.
excerpt: Discretes Input Single bit Type of access Read-Only Coils Single bit Read-Write

front: How does a Modbus holding register differ from an input register?
back: Both are 16-bit words, but a holding register is read-write, while an input register is read-only.
excerpt: Input Registers 16-bit word Read-Only Holding Registers 16-bit word Read-Write
mnemonic: Holding registers hold values you may change; input registers only bring readings in.

front: What two parts make up a Modbus protocol data unit (PDU)?
back: A one-byte function code, which names the action to perform, followed by the data for that action.
excerpt: mb_req_pdu = Function code (1 byte) + request data (n bytes)

front: What does Modbus function code 03 ask a server to do?
back: Read the contents of a contiguous block of holding registers and return them.
excerpt: This function code is used to read the contents of a contiguous block of holding registers in a remote device.

front: How do you calculate the protocol data unit (PDU) address of a Modbus data item numbered X?
back: PDU address = X − 1 (items are numbered from 1, addresses start at 0).
excerpt: The previous figure shows that a MODBUS data numbered X is addressed in the MODBUS PDU X-1.
mnemonic: Item number 1 lives at address 0: subtract one before sending.
